name: Padoe
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: Stress is always on the penultimate syllable, regardless of suffixes added to the root word, whether derivational, inflectional or aspectual (cf. Martens 1988 and Barr 1988, for Uma and Da'a, where the stress placement is not as straightforward).

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict penultimate (penultimate stress) rests on a verbatim, page-confirmed statement in the only dedicated phonology of Padoe (Karhunen 1991:188 §6), which we hold as a text-layer PDF; the statement explicitly covers suffixed/derived words and the examples show stress moving rightward with suffixation, so word domain and strict penult are correct. Three further held sources (Mead 1998:97, Mead 1999:101/103, Vuorinen 1995) independently agree and Mead 1999 identifies Karhunen 1991 as the phonological description of Padoe. Nothing in Glottolog's bibliography outranks it; no works still to obtain. The record's 'grade' field is blank although the quote is verbatim-primary and confirmed — only action suggested is to fill/upgrade the strength of the evidence. was created and is empty.
